items.title: The dimension of a fibre at a point is at most the sum of the fibre dimensions along the composite, with equality under flatness
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a composite of locally finite type morphisms the fibre dimension at a point is at most the sum of the two relative fibre dimensions, with equality when the local ring of the innermost fibre is flat over the local ring of the fibre over the middle base (statement lines 5395-5407). The counted proof is short and complete: it applies additivity of transcendence degree over the tower of residue field extensions, uses the description of the fibre dimension at a point to rewrite the claim as an inequality between local rings of the two fibres, and concludes both the inequality and the flat equality from the cited local algebra statements, noting that flatness of the ambient local rings implies the required flatness (proof lines 5409-5422). It is H2: the reduction is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the fibre dimension formula and the two algebra statements.
